name: FL-23
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 9 points on the partisan baseline
Frankel holds a massive cash advantage ($1.2M vs $34K) with outside support
Prediction markets price Frankel at 94-95% to win
No public polling available, so the forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Frankel: a 9-point Democratic district, incumbency, and a dominant fundraising edge over challenger Deborah Adeimy, while both major markets price her near 95%. With no polling to contradict that picture, the race stays safely Democratic.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for Adeimy or a strong Republican environment in South Florida could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Lois Frankel seeks another term in this Palm Beach-area district that leans Democratic by about nine points. She enters the general election with a commanding financial position, having raised $2.3 million and holding $1.2 million on hand, plus modest outside support. Republican challenger Deborah Adeimy has raised about $163,000 with limited cash remaining and no reported outside backing.

No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive. Prediction markets on both major platforms give Frankel roughly a 94-95 percent chance of winning. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and the money gap makes this a safe Democratic seat, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty about the exact margin.
